summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: big-O notation and worst-case time of Turing machines, polynomials and complex numbers, and the calculus the degree requires (limits, convergence of sequences and series, basic integrals). The same degree is taken to include introductory discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, induction, sets, graphs, recurrences) and a first course in linear algebra over the reals (vectors, subspaces, matrices, elimination, dot products), each at introductory depth. Fields in the abstract sense, tensor products, bilinear forms over general fields, Gaussian integers and the Chinese remainder theorem are not assumed.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers in which a and b are identified when they differ by a multiple of a fixed modulus c, written a ≡ b (mod c).

known.name: Prime numbers and greatest common divisors
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and itself, and gcd(a, b) is the largest integer dividing both a and b; a and b are coprime when their gcd is 1.

known.name: Arithmetic modulo 2 and XOR
known.gloss: The set {0, 1} with addition given by exclusive-or (sum modulo 2) and multiplication given by AND, which is the arithmetic of bits and parity.

known.name: Dyadic rationals
known.gloss: Rational numbers of the form a/2^k with a an integer and k a nonnegative integer, i.e. the numbers with finite binary expansions.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces, bases and dimension
known.gloss: A vector space is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication; a basis is a linearly independent spanning set, and the dimension is the number of vectors in any basis.

known.name: Linear maps, matrix operations and invertibility
known.gloss: A linear map sends sums to sums and scalar multiples to scalar multiples and is represented by a matrix; a square matrix is invertible when it has a two-sided inverse, and the kernel is the set of vectors sent to zero.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: The procedure that reduces a matrix by elementary row operations to echelon form, whose pivots determine solutions and rank.

known.name: Triangular matrices
known.gloss: A square matrix whose entries above (lower-triangular) or below (upper-triangular) the diagonal are all zero.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality in R^n
known.gloss: The dot product of two real vectors is the sum of products of corresponding entries; two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero, and an orthonormal basis consists of mutually orthogonal unit vectors.

known.name: Permutations of a finite set
known.gloss: A bijection from a finite set of indices to itself, which rearranges the entries of a sequence or array.

known.name: Finite sets, subsets and intersections
known.gloss: The intersection of two sets is the set of their common elements, the cardinality counts elements, and the binomial coefficient (n choose k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set.

known.name: Graphs
known.gloss: A graph is a set of vertices together with a set of edges, each joining two vertices, and two vertices are adjacent when they are joined by an edge.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for all integers n by proving a base case and that the statement for smaller values implies it for n.

known.name: Recurrence relations and divide-and-conquer recursion
known.gloss: An equation that defines a quantity, such as the running time of a recursive algorithm, in terms of its values on smaller inputs.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The floor of x is the largest integer not exceeding x and the ceiling is the smallest integer not less than x.

known.name: Logarithms base 2
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm lg x is the exponent to which 2 must be raised to give x, which is the number of binary digits needed to represent x up to one.

known.name: Big-Omega and big-Theta notation
known.gloss: f = Ω(g) means f is bounded below by a positive constant multiple of g for all large inputs, and f = Θ(g) means f is both O(g) and Ω(g).

known.name: Limits and convergence of sequences and series
known.gloss: A sequence converges to L when its terms eventually stay arbitrarily close to L, and a series converges when its partial sums converge.

known.name: Geometric series
aliases: sum of powers of a ratio
known.gloss: The series a + ar + ar^2 + ... whose partial sums equal a(1 - r^(k+1))/(1 - r), converging when |r| < 1 to a/(1 - r).

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: The iteration x_{k+1} = x_k - f(x_k)/f'(x_k) that approximates a root of f by repeatedly following tangent lines.

known.name: Worst-case time complexity of a Turing machine
known.gloss: For a Turing machine, the maximum number of steps it takes on any input of length n, viewed as a function of n.
